decisions.executionNote: Turn both open grippers downward while moving forward and maintaining elbow-up continuity; establish overhead approaches for red pepper and right chocolate bar.
Use smaller initial pitch and translation increments after zero-execution IK rejection.
Continue overhead pitch and approach the red pepper and outer chocolate; keep open and pause above the surface to refine alignment.
Fine-align and lower the left gripper around the red pepper; rotate the right gripper across the chocolate bar's short dimension before descending.
Close on the red pepper and make a short retention lift. Fine-align the right gripper and lower slowly onto the outer chocolate bar.
Red pepper appears retained. Raise it above the white basket rim and start the transfer; close the aligned right gripper on the bar and lift to check retention.
Both objects remain between fingers. Use smaller forward increments and a slight forward tool tilt to preserve reach margin while approaching the white and red baskets.
Release the red pepper within the left basket and begin retreating. Advance the retained chocolate over the right basket using a forward tilt rather than extending the elbow fully.
Release the first bar inside the right basket. Move the open left gripper toward the yellow pepper and retreat the right gripper before approaching the remaining bar.
Approach the yellow pepper from above with the left arm and the remaining diagonal bar with the right, maintaining separate workspaces and open grippers.
Center and close gently around the yellow pepper; remove residual right-tool tilt while lowering toward the second bar. Retention will be checked visually.
Allow the left grip to settle and make a short vertical retention lift. Fine-center the remaining chocolate bar and close the right gripper without lateral dragging.
Lift both closed grasps clear of the table, then separate laterally toward their respective baskets. Check that the yellow pepper and second bar follow the grippers.
Transport the retained yellow pepper toward the white basket and second chocolate toward the red basket, keeping both above the rims with modest forward tilt.
Move each object farther inside its assigned basket, lower slightly, and open both grippers to release without sweeping the contents.
Both peppers and both bars are visibly in their baskets. Approach the yellow car with the left arm while beginning the right arm's open-gripper return toward origin.
Replan the zero-execution rejection with a slower right-arm retreat from its near-extended pose; left arm continues the yellow-car approach.
Refine the yellow-car alignment and lower the open left gripper onto its sides. Continue returning the right arm with smaller continuous pose changes.
Close on the yellow car, settle, and perform a short vertical retention lift; finish the right arm's return to its starting pose.
Yellow car appears retained. Raise before moving toward the middle basket. Slow the final right-arm reset after its continuity interruption.
Carry the retained yellow car over the left half of the middle basket, using forward wrist tilt to avoid full extension. Complete the right arm's final small reset adjustments.
Release the yellow car deeper inside the middle basket, then withdraw the open left gripper. Keep the reset right arm parked.
Yellow car is in the middle basket. Approach the last white car with the left gripper rotated to span its narrow sides; keep the right arm at origin.
The last descent tracked poorly near the basket rim. Narrow the open grip slightly, correct tool tilt, and approach the white car with small increments away from the rim.
Back the left gripper away from the blue rim and center the white car in the wrist view before another small descent; avoid pushing against the persistent obstruction.
Lift clear of the basket rim before correcting the approach; reduce the open jaw span so the rear finger can clear the rim during the next descent.
With the tool now clear and nearly vertical, descend to the white car with reduced jaw opening, keeping the rear finger outside the blue basket rim.
The narrowed finger is landing on the car rather than alongside it. Lift and switch to an end-to-end grasp so both fingers descend clear of the nearby basket rim.
Lower the fully open gripper around the car's front and rear ends, using the unobstructed approach and a small forward centering correction.
Close around the white car's ends, allow the grip to settle, then lift slightly away from the basket rim to check retention.
Raise the closed white-car grasp above the rim and verify retention before carrying it forward into the middle basket.
The white car did not remain held. Reopen and retry the end grasp lower on the body, keeping the gripper clear of the basket wall.
The wrist housing appears blocked by the basket. Pull the EE backward while tilting the fingers forward, keeping the grasp point on the car and lowering clear of the rim.
Close around the exposed front and rear body surfaces from the angled approach, settle, and make a very short lift to test retention before transport.
Lift the closed end grasp straight upward, slightly away from the rim, to verify that the white car is now retained before transfer.
The end grasp slipped again. Change to a narrower side-body grasp while retaining the backward-offset wrist position that avoids the basket housing collision.
Use the wrist view to move the side grasp backward off the roof and away from the blue rim, centering the body between the fingers before closing.
The white car is centered between the side fingers with clear tracking. Lower slightly to engage the body rather than the roof and close without translating.
Settle the side-body grasp, then lift vertically without changing orientation to check white-car retention.
The car again stayed on the table. Recenter the side grasp onto the wider middle body and descend farther below the roof, accounting for the forward-tilted finger offset.
Close the lower side grasp and withdraw slightly from the rim with minimal lift, checking whether the car follows before lifting higher.
The car followed the short backward withdrawal. Keep the grip closed and make a slow vertical retention lift without changing orientation.
The white car now stays fixed between the fingers through the lift. Raise it above the middle basket rim and align over its left half, keeping the same grasp orientation.
Carry the retained white car over the middle basket, using a small forward tilt and modest lowering to maintain elbow-up reach margin.
Release the retained white car inside the middle basket, wait for it to settle, and begin withdrawing the open left gripper.
All six objects are visibly in their assigned baskets. Withdraw the open left arm and smoothly restore its starting orientation; correct small right-arm home drift.
Continue the open left arm's smooth return toward its original pose, preserving configuration continuity and leaving the sorted contents undisturbed.
Finish returning the left arm to its observed starting pose with both grippers open; make a small right-home correction while keeping all sorted objects undisturbed.
